body.statement:
Let \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\), equivalently \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)\), denote the class imposing aggregate support and the correlation restriction only on \(\{d,e\}\), and let \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) impose those armwise restrictions for every \(a\in\mathcal A\).  The class definitions contain no restriction coupling distinct potential-outcome arms.  If \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\ne\varnothing\), then, for \(a\in\{d,e\}\),
\[
 \{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},
\]
and
\[
 \{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\}
 =\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\}.
\]
Their arm-mean closures are \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\), and their ATE closure is \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\).  In particular, conditional product coupling establishes joint endpoint approximation rather than merely subtracting marginal outer bounds.  When \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), the two classes are identical.
body.justification: The coupling establishes joint target-arm attainment and also shows when the target-arm calculation is faithful to Ban--Kédagni's all-arm published class.
body.gap: Park2025 treats joint attainment under MIV plus MTR; it does not supply this conditional-product witness for armwise SDC, exact aggregate support, or extension from target-arm to all-arm restrictions.
body.consumer: Finite-valued-treatment users may report the exact ATE closure for the published all-arm class when that class is nonempty, while binary-treatment applications obtain the result without a class distinction.
body.proof_tex:
Define the target-arm causal identified sets
\[
 \Theta_{a,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)
 =\{\theta_a(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},\qquad
 \Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)
 =\{\Delta_{d,e}(Q):Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\},                       \tag{38}
\]
and define \(\Theta_{a,\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) and \(\Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) by replacing \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\) in (38) with \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\).  These are causal sets; the observed-law functionals \(\mathcal I_a^r(P)\) and \(\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P)\) will be shown to equal their closures, not defined to do so.

We first establish sharpness for the target-arm class.  Fix eligible signs \(b\in\mathcal B_d^r(P)\) and \(h\in\mathcal B_e^r(P)\), and choose exactly support-admissible marginal completions for the two arms.  Let \(K_{a,j}\) denote the chosen conditional law of \(Y_a\) in cell \(j\).  On a factual cell \(j\in\mathcal O_a\), compatibility and consistency require \(Y_a=Y\); on a missing cell, \(K_{a,j}\) has support \([\ell_a,u_a]\) and the chosen feasible mean.

Draw \((Y,D,Z)\sim P\).  Conditional on \((Y,D,Z)\), set \(Y_a=Y\) whenever \(D=a\), and for every missing target arm draw \(Y_a\) from \(K_{a,j}\), independently across arms given the observed data.  Each target potential outcome then has exactly its selected cellwise marginal law.  Consequently, the construction preserves \(Q_{Y,D,Z}=P\), consistency, each aggregate support, and each armwise score moment.  Conditional independence is only a coupling device and is not imposed on the model.

It follows that every pair of exactly attainable means from the selected branches is jointly attainable in \(\mathcal Q^r(P)\).  By \(\text{thm:support-eligibility}\), those attainable means are dense in
\[
 [L_{d,b}^r(P),U_{d,b}^r(P)]
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 [L_{e,h}^r(P),U_{e,h}^r(P)].
\]
Their differences are therefore dense in
\[
 [L_{d,b}^r(P)-U_{e,h}^r(P),
   U_{d,b}^r(P)-L_{e,h}^r(P)].                                  \tag{39}
\]
Conversely, \(\text{lem:branch-reduction}\) places the two means induced by every \(Q\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\) in closures of eligible branch images.  The finite union over \((b,h)\), together with \(\text{def:arm-closure}\) and \(\text{def:ate-closure}\), therefore gives
\[
 \operatorname{cl}\Theta_{a,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)=\mathcal I_a^r(P),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{cl}\Theta_{\Delta,\mathrm{tar}}^r(P)=\mathcal I_\Delta^r(P). \tag{19a}
\]

We now compare the target-arm and all-arm classes.  The definition gives \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\subseteq\mathcal Q^r(P)\), so both Ban--K\'edagni identified sets are contained in their target-arm counterparts.  For the reverse inclusion, use the assumed nonemptiness to fix \(Q^0\in\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\), and fix an arbitrary \(Q^1\in\mathcal Q^r(P)\).  In each observed cell, retain from \(Q^1\) the conditional marginal kernels of \(Y_d\) and \(Y_e\), and retain from \(Q^0\) the conditional marginal kernel of every \(Y_a\) with \(a\notin\{d,e\}\).  Draw \((Y,D,Z)\sim P\); set \(Y_D=Y\); and, conditional on the observed data, product-couple all remaining potential outcomes from the retained kernels.

For each target arm, the resulting law has the same cellwise marginal kernels as \(Q^1\), so it preserves that law's target means, score restrictions, and aggregate supports.  For every untargeted arm, it has the same cellwise marginal kernels as \(Q^0\), so it preserves the corresponding all-arm restrictions.  Compatibility and consistency hold by construction.  Because the maintained class contains no restriction involving two distinct potential-outcome arms, no defining condition is changed by replacing the original cross-arm dependence with this conditional product coupling.  The resulting law \(\widetilde Q\) therefore belongs to \(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{BK}}^r(P)\) and satisfies
\[
 \theta_d(\widetilde Q)=\theta_d(Q^1),\qquad
 \theta_e(\widetilde Q)=\theta_e(Q^1),\qquad
 \Delta_{d,e}(\widetilde Q)=\Delta_{d,e}(Q^1).                    \tag{19b}
\]
Since \(Q^1\) was arbitrary, (19b) proves the reverse inclusions and hence equality of the exact identified sets.  Combining that equality with (19a) proves the asserted sharp closures.  If \(\mathcal A=\{d,e\}\), there are no untargeted arms, so the two class definitions coincide.  The nonempty all-arm premise is essential to the extension argument: without \(Q^0\), admissible untargeted-arm kernels need not exist.
